def.description: Specialist panel reviews the proposed M3 loop-driver + morning report + routing + state design for the IRIS optimization loop; arbiter reports consensus or consolidated critique.

branches.task:
METHODOLOGY / COHERENCE REVIEW (round {args.round}).

The IRIS optimization loop has two locked halves: MEASURE (a 3-layer eval, DL-0022) and EXPLORE (a candidate-generator that emits a ranked top-5 with confounder cards, DL-0023). This is the THIRD piece: M3 — the loop-driver that assembles the generator output into a morning report, gates it on human approval, routes approved items, and persists loop state across runs.

PROPOSAL:
{args.proposal}

Prior-round critique to check is addressed:
{args.prior_critique}

Judge ONLY through a systems-coherence / decision-integrity lens: (1) Is the STATE MODEL sound — is there a single source of truth, and can a landed candidate be double-applied, a quarantine clock double-advanced, or the change-counter desynced from reality? (2) Is a manual re-run IDEMPOTENT and crash-resumable, or can a mid-run failure double-emit / double-route? (3) Is the morning report DECISION-COMPLETE — does a human have exactly what they need to approve/reject each of the 5 without leaving the report? (4) Does the landed->ledger->baseline-refresh cycle actually close the measure/explore loop, or are there gaps (e.g. a merged PR that never gets marked landed)? (5) Is the delta-vs-baseline attribution to a batch of <=5 candidates a real signal or hand-waving? Output AGREE or OBJECT per element with a concrete fix.

args.proposal:
IRIS optimization loop — M3 LOOP-DRIVER + MORNING REPORT + ROUTING + STATE, v1 (r4 FINAL). Measure=DL-0022; explore=DL-0023; top-5 cap=DL-0020; portable loop=DL-0021. Loop lives in dotdev; SUT is IRIS (classdojo/iris). [tunable]=build constant; OPEN=human-input non-blocking.

PURPOSE: assemble the generator's ranked top-5 into a morning report, gate on genuine human approval, route approved items to real targets, persist loop state across runs. v1 manual; auto mode deferred.

A. STATE: committed JSON loop/state.json on a dedicated `loop-state` branch in dotdev (NOT main — DL-0011 blocks main pushes; loop-state exempt from main-protection; first-run preflight `gh api repos/johnalexwelch/dotdev/rulesets` confirms). Tracks: baseline pointer {pinned IRIS commit, judge model, capture date, per-case pass map, P10 floor, permutation null}; per-case quarantine clocks; approved-not-yet-landed; pending-implementation (Type 4/5 issue-routed items awaiting landing confirmation); landed ledger {id, type, diff hash, approval ts, landed ts, merge entry {repo, sha} OR issue entry {repo, issue_url, closed_at, human_confirmed:true}, human_edited:bool immutable}; change-counter; sentinel net time-series; suite version; fixture-gap pointer. Read→append→commit each run. Validate schema + SHA-256 checksum of canonicalized JSON; REFUSE malformed/mismatched state. Hand-edits via `loop state edit` (validate + rehash; BLOCKS changes to human_edited on existing entries) or `loop state rehash`. v1 SINGLE-OPERATOR + single-machine file lock (distributed lock deferred).

B. RUN / IDEMPOTENCY: manual `loop run`, keyed {suite version + baseline pointer + IRIS-commit + date}. Lifecycle started → stub_posted:{url} → routed:{ids, pr_urls, issue_urls} → emitted. Same-key re-run idempotent; a crashed run resumes via the §E crash-resume probe. Quarantine clocks advance ONLY at emitted. STALE-RUN CHECK: at run start, if any run in state has status≠emitted and date≠today, warn listing the stale run key + its routed-but-open PR/issue URLs (visibility only, no action).

C. REPORT (read-only, NOT approval surface): loop/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md + a dotdev issue (label loop-report), posted in TWO stages: (1) at stub_posted — a lightweight tracking stub (date, IRIS commit, 'report pending'); (2) at emitted — full report committed to loop/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md on loop-state AND the stub issue updated with full content incl route URLs. Sections: (1) HEADER — date, IRIS commit, baseline freshness + changes-since-baseline, judge model, suite version, counts, budget. (2) LOOP-HEALTH — sentinel net vs prior run (PASS/HALT), generator≠judge; on FAILURE emit ONLY health + zero candidates (precedes candidate processing; no --force/--skip-health). (3) TOP-5 (net desc) — rank, net, type+blast, hypothesis, rendered diff, target cluster, full confounder card (cluster N, holdout N, permutation p, FDR q, cross-lane note, SOLE-DOMAIN + flags), fully-resolved route path (PR/issue URL); HIGH-blast/cross-lane as a distinct callout above the approval commands. (4) CANNOT-VALIDATE (separate, below the 5; informational; NOT `loop approve`-eligible in v1; author a fixture if real else `loop reject`). (5) FIXTURE-GAP queue status (count, oldest age, backlog-halt). (6) BLIND-SPOT lines — metric-disambiguation EVAL-INVISIBLE count + examples; budget-exceeded clusters. (7) STALENESS ALERT — 'N candidates approved >30d have not landed; `loop status`.' (Type 4/5 PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION items shown with a distinct [PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION] marker; a review prompt, not an error.) (8) CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner — if unresolved, list suspect batch + IRIS SHA at prior baseline vs refresh baseline + instructions; persists every report until rollback OR `loop dismiss-regression <date>` + rationale. (9) FOOTER — loop approve/reject/edit <date> <id>; 'pending approvals expire when the next loop run completes reconcile.'

D. APPROVAL GATE (CLI, per-candidate): `loop approve <date> <id>` writes {authenticated operator identity, ts, exact diff hash}; fails APPROVAL-DEADLINE-EXPIRED if a newer run key exists. ROUTING EXECUTES IMMEDIATELY WITHIN `loop approve` after the approval record: path-existence validation (Types 1/2/3), two-phase artifact creation, URL written to state — all complete before the command returns. `loop reject <date> <id>` writes explicit rejection (also valid to close a stale approved-not-yet-landed or pending-implementation entry). `loop edit <date> <id>` opens the diff in $EDITOR; on save validate + rehash, write {original_hash, edited_hash, human_edited:true}, then REQUIRE a separate `loop approve`. DEFAULT=REJECT: no approval record by deadline = NOT routed (no rubber-stamp by omission, no batch-approve, no --auto-approve in v1). ROUTING DEADLINE: implicitly rejected when the NEXT `loop run` completes reconcile.

E. ROUTING (approved → target; one artifact per candidate, never batched; two-phase): write status=routing, routing_id=<id> BEFORE creation. CRASH-RESUME PROBE on resume: PRs `gh pr list --head loop/<date>-<id> --repo <target> --json url --state open`; issues `gh issue list --repo <target> --label loop/<date>-<id> --state open --json url`; if found, record URL + continue without recreating; else create. PATH-EXISTENCE VALIDATION for Types 1/2/3: `gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<resolved-path>?ref=<iris-commit>`; if missing, abort ROUTE-TARGET-STALE before two-phase. Write the artifact URL to state before advancing. Type 1 prompt/instruction → PR into classdojo/iris at the path from loop/config/iris-prompt-targets.yaml ({sql_generation,findings_prose,system_prefix}→paths), branch loop/<date>-<id>, body = hypothesis + confounder card + report link + [HUMAN-EDITED] if applicable. Type 2 reflection/habit → PR into iris (v1 PR-only), scoped {scope, scope_key}, path from iris-habit-targets.yaml (OD-2 first, else ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2). Type 3 tool schema/description → PR into iris at the path from iris-tool-targets.yaml; REQUIRES a {target_tool_path} field. Type 4 retrieval-corpus → human-judgment ISSUE in classdojo/iris (EVAL-INVISIBLE), label loop/<date>-<id>; marks PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION. Type 5 routing/findings-pipeline code → ISSUE in classdojo/iris (needs implementation), triage-labeled, label loop/<date>-<id>; marks PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION. Fixture-gap note → ISSUE in classdojo/iris (fixtures at backend/src/iris/eval/), label fixture-audit + loop/<date>-<id>, links to the dotdev report. Every artifact carries candidate id + report link + confounder card + [HUMAN-EDITED] marker, links back to the ledger.

F. LANDED → LEDGER → BASELINE: `loop reconcile` runs automatically as the FIRST step of every run. PR landing: merged PRs in classdojo/iris with branch prefix loop/ AND base:default-branch; per newly-merged PR extract candidate id from the branch, verify merge {repo, sha} not already in the ledger (dedup on repo AND sha), secondary duplicate-candidate-id check (conflict warning, not silent increment), mark landed, increment change-counter. Issue landing (Type 4/5 PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION): (a) auto-detect `gh issue list --repo classdojo/iris --label loop/<date>-<id> --state closed` → mark landed {repo, issue_url, closed_at} + increment; OR (b) explicit `loop mark-landed <date> <id>` → {repo, issue_url, human_confirmed:true} + increment (for issues implemented via a separate non-loop PR). 'landed' = merged-to-default-branch (PR) or issue-closed/mark-landed (issue); loop approve = human-approval event, merge/close = landing event; no second approval. At change-counter=[5 tunable] OR judge/IRIS model bump, PROPOSE a baseline refresh (never auto); human confirms → capture records a new baseline pointer + resets quarantine clocks + re-quarantines the pre-refresh holdout set (DL-0023 §E).

G. PROVENANCE: at each refresh, the DL-0023 §J delta-vs-last-baseline check attributes per-case regressions to the batch of ≤5 landed candidates since the last refresh (batch granularity, known limitation); human-edited candidates included with a [HUMAN-EDITED] flag. A newly-regressed case raises CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION + surfaces the suspect batch (with IRIS SHA delta: prior baseline commit vs refresh commit) for a human rollback decision (revert the suspect iris PRs + `loop set-counter <n>` + re-capture). CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION persists in the LOOP-HEALTH banner until rollback OR `loop dismiss-regression <date>` + written rationale (dismissal ≠ rollback).

H. SECRETS / ACCESS: scoring needs warehouse creds + LLM keys (--execute --e2e). v1 operator local creds from env/secret store; keys NEVER enter state, reports, PR/issue bodies, or logs. Preflight verifies write access to classdojo/iris (branch + PR + issue) BEFORE scoring; failure aborts with a credential error ('preflight failed: {service}', no usernames/hostnames/warehouse names). Secret-pattern scrubbing via a curated deny-list (sk-*, sk-ant-*, AKIA*, xoxb-*, postgres://, mysql://, mongodb://, hooks.slack.com, and any [A-Za-z0-9]{20,} adjacent to key/token/secret/password) on all LLM outputs before report/PR. [OPEN: local vs CI runner].

I. AUTO MODE (deferred, slice 6): v1 fully human-gated; no auto-approval path until a multi-run track record + trusted sentinel/health.

J. RECOVERY RUNBOOK — LOOP PR FAILS IRIS CI: run `loop reject <date> <id>` (explicit rejection, clears the approved-not-yet-landed entry, lets the next run's generator re-cluster from the same failure class if it persists). Do NOT hand-push fixes to the loop/ branch — reject and let the generator re-propose.

OPEN DECISIONS (human input, non-blocking for design; blocking for their route type at runtime): OD-1 iris prompt file paths; OD-2 habit/reflection store path (→ iris-habit-targets.yaml before Type 2 routing); OD-3 iris branch-protection effect on loop/ PRs (→ §J runbook); OD-4 local vs CI runner.

WORKED EXAMPLE: run 2026-08-01, IRIS@abc123, baseline fresh (2 changes since). STALE-RUN check passes. Reconcile first (no new merges). Generator emits 3 validated; sentinel PASS. Stub issue posted. #1 engagement-attribution habit (net 3, MEDIUM, [SOLE-DOMAIN]) → `loop approve 2026-08-01 1` → path-check passes → two-phase route within the approve command → PR to iris at the resolved habit path, branch loop/2026-08-01-1 → URL written → approve returns. #2 Type 5 code → `loop approve 2026-08-01 2` → issue in iris labeled loop/2026-08-01-2 → PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION. #3 `loop edit 2026-08-01 3` then `loop approve 2026-08-01 3` → routed [HUMAN-EDITED]. Report committed; stub updated with URLs; → emitted. Next day 2026-08-02 reconcile completes → unapproved 2026-08-01 candidates expire. A week later #1 merges → reconcile marks landed (repo+sha), counter 2→3. Dev implements #2 and closes the issue → reconcile auto-detects OR `loop mark-landed 2026-08-01 2` → 3→4. At 5 the driver proposes a refresh; human confirms; capture resets quarantine per §E.
args.prior_critique: Round-3 folded fixes to CONFIRM (arbiter critique:none, held false only to re-review): (1) Type-4/5 route to ISSUES (no merge event) → new PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION status + landed via issue-closure auto-scan OR explicit `loop mark-landed <date> <id>` {repo, issue_url, human_confirmed}; issue-routed items increment change-counter only when landed via either path; (2) two-stage report: `stub_posted` (date, IRIS commit, 'report pending') at start, full report + route URLs committed + stub updated at `emitted`; lifecycle renamed issue_posted→stub_posted; (3) routing executes IMMEDIATELY within `loop approve` (path-check + two-phase creation + URL written to state before approve returns) — not deferred, closes the approve/expire race; (4) STALE-RUN check at run start warns on any prior run with status≠emitted and date≠today, listing routed-but-open URLs (visibility only); (5) removed spurious dotdev from the reconcile PR query — all loop/ PRs go to classdojo/iris; issues carry label loop/<date>-<id> + issue crash-resume probe `gh issue list --label loop/<date>-<id> --state open`; (6) expanded secret deny-list (sk-ant-*, xoxb-*, postgres://, mysql://, mongodb://, hooks.slack.com, [A-Za-z0-9]{20,} adjacent to key/token/secret/password); (7) CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner adds IRIS SHA delta (prior baseline vs refresh). OPEN (non-blocking): OD-1..OD-4. CONFIRM: fixes correctly integrated, no NEW contradiction/blocker. If NO material change needed, return consensus:true.

panel.output:
### [1/3] critic

## Critique

**Summary:** The proposal should not stand as-is — two concrete control-flow gaps survive round-3, both introduced by that round's own fixes. The other three elements are sound.

---

### Element-by-element verdict

---

**1. STATE MODEL — AGREE**

The dedup guard on `(repo, sha)` correctly prevents double-application of a merged PR; the secondary candidate-id check is a reasonable integrity alarm without silently inflating the counter. Quarantine clocks are gated on a single terminal event (`emitted`), so double-advancement requires double-reaching `emitted`, which same-key idempotency prevents. The SHA-256 checksum + REFUSE-on-mismatch policy closes the file-corruption vector. The single-operator file lock is adequate for v1 scope.

*Residual (non-blocking):* There is no formal crash-resume probe for `reconcile` itself — only for routing. A crash mid-reconcile (after detecting a merge, before committing state) would re-detect the same merge on the next run. The dedup guard handles this correctly, but it does so implicitly rather than through the named crash-resume protocol that covers routing.

---

**2. IDEMPOTENCY / CRASH-RESUMABILITY — OBJECT**

**Gap introduced by round-3 fix (2) — two-stage report / `emitted` transition trigger is undefined.**

The lifecycle in §B is `started → stub_posted → routed → emitted`, and §C says "at emitted — full report committed…AND the stub issue updated with full content incl route URLs." Quarantine clocks advance **only** at `emitted`. But the proposal never states *what command or event causes the run to transition to `emitted`*.

The worked example implies `emitted` fires after all three candidates are decided (approve/reject), suggesting it fires within the last `loop approve` or `loop reject` invocation. But this is not stated. Three incoherent alternatives remain open simultaneously:

- (a) The last `loop approve/reject` for a run checks "any undecided candidates remaining?" and fires report-commit + `emitted` if none. This is the worked-example interpretation but is never specified in §D.
- (b) A separate `loop finalize` command triggers it. No such command exists in the spec.
- (c) The next `loop run`'s reconcile step expires undecided candidates and then finalizes the prior run. This would mean the STALE-RUN CHECK fires first, and reconcile of day N+1 emits day N's report — but this double-duty for reconcile is not mentioned in §F.

**Why this matters for idempotency:** Without knowing what triggers `emitted`, you cannot reason about whether a crashed `loop approve` would leave the run permanently in `routed` (report never committed, clocks never advanced) or double-commit the report if re-run. The crash-resume probe in §E covers artifact creation inside `loop approve` but says nothing about the report-commit step.

**Fix:** Add one sentence to §B (or §D) specifying the trigger: "When all candidates in the run have an approval or rejection record, the report is committed to `loop-state`, the stub issue is updated, and the run transitions to `emitted`; this check runs within every `loop approve` and `loop reject` invocation after writing the record."

---

**3. MORNING REPORT DECISION-COMPLETE — AGREE**

The report carries, per candidate: hypothesis, rendered diff, target cluster, confounder card (cluster N, holdout N, permutation p, FDR q, blast tier, cross-lane note, interpreted flags), fully-resolved route path, and `loop approve/reject/edit <date> <id>` commands. HIGH-blast items surface as a distinct callout above the commands. This is sufficient for a human to decide without leaving the report.

*Residual (non-blocking):* For Type 5 (code changes), "rendered diff" in a markdown report may not carry enough syntactic context for a meaningful approval, but the human is approving *routing* (create an issue in IRIS), not the code quality — the actual code review happens at the PR/issue level. This is architecturally correct. Type 2 without OD-2 resolved surfaces as `ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2`, which is visible. No blocking gap.

---

**4. LANDED→LEDGER→BASELINE CYCLE — OBJECT**

**Gap introduced by round-3 fix (1) — Type 4/5 auto-detect via `--state closed` conflates implemented with closed-as-rejected.**

§F defines issue landing as: `gh issue list --repo classdojo/iris --label loop/<date>-<id> --state closed` → mark landed, increment change-counter.

GitHub's `--state closed` matches any issue closure, including "won't fix," "not planned," or "duplicate." A developer who closes a PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION issue without implementing it would cause `reconcile` to mark it landed and increment the change-counter. If five such events accumulate, the driver proposes a baseline refresh against an IRIS that has not actually changed. The new baseline would be identical to the old one, wasting a scored run and producing a spurious empty delta. Worse, the CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION check would compare two baselines from the same IRIS commit and might surface noise-level case flips as a CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner.

The `human_confirmed:true` field on explicit `loop mark-landed` is the correct guard, but auto-detect bypasses it.

**Concrete counterexample from the worked example:** Suppose a developer triages issue `loop/2026-08-01-2` (Type 5 code change) and closes it as "needs more scoping." On the next `loop run`, reconcile sees state=closed, marks the candidate landed, increments counter 2→3. At some later run the counter reaches 5 and the driver proposes a refresh. The refresh captures a baseline with zero code changes from that batch. The cumulative regression check compares an unchanged IRIS against itself.

**Fix (smallest):** For auto-detect, also require the issue to have a `loop-landed` label (or equivalent) added by the implementer, rather than relying on close state alone. Alternatively, demote auto-detect entirely: require explicit `loop mark-landed <date> <id>` for all Type 4/5 items and document that auto-detect is disabled for issues due to close-reason ambiguity. The `--state closed` probe is still useful as a *prompt* (surfaced in `loop status`), just not as an automatic counter increment.

---

**5. BATCH ATTRIBUTION (≤5 CANDIDATES) — AGREE**

For the change-counter=5 trigger (same model, judge temp=0, pinned model version): re-running the suite against a new IRIS baseline and comparing case-by-case pass maps is a genuine regression signal. If a case newly fails, something in the ≤5 landed changes caused it; batch granularity means you can't isolate which one without bisection, but the CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION flag correctly demands a human rollback decision. This is not hand-waving — it's a known, explicitly-acknowledged limitation with a stated recovery path (revert the suspect iris PRs + `loop set-counter` + re-capture).

*Residual:* The model-bump trigger introduces model-behavior noise into the attribution (case flip may reflect model change, not candidate change). This is acknowledged and accepted. No new objection.

---

### Required corrections (both block design lock)

| # | Section | Fix |
|---|---------|-----|
| 2 | §B and/or §D | Name the exact event that triggers `emitted`: "When the last candidate in the run receives an approval or rejection record, the run transitions to `emitted`, committing the full report and updating the stub issue. If candidates remain undecided at the start of the next `loop run`, reconcile expires them and fires this same transition for the prior run." |
| 4 | §F (issue landing) | Remove the automatic change-counter increment from `--state closed` auto-detect. Either require a `loop-landed` label added by the implementer, or disable auto-detect and require explicit `loop mark-landed` for all Type 4/5 items. |

### Questions (none block progress)

OD-1 through OD-4 remain correctly classified as non-blocking. No new questions.

---

### [2/3] analyst

## Analysis

### R3-Folded Fixes Confirmation

All 7 fixes are correctly integrated with no new internal contradictions:

| Fix | Location in Design | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Type-4/5 → ISSUES + PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION | §E types 4/5; §F issue landing; §C report §7 | ✓ |
| Two-stage report (stub_posted / emitted) | §C two stages; §B lifecycle | ✓ |
| Routing executes immediately within `loop approve` | §D explicit statement; §E crash-resume | ✓ |
| STALE-RUN check at run start | §B "at run start, if any run…" | ✓ |
| classdojo/iris-only in reconcile PR query | §F "merged PRs in classdojo/iris"; §E issue crash-resume `--repo classdojo/iris` | ✓ |
| Expanded secret deny-list | §H deny-list entries | ✓ |
| CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner adds IRIS SHA delta | §G "prior baseline commit vs refresh commit" | ✓ |

---

### Known (design evidence)

- `iris-prompt-targets.yaml` lives in dotdev and maps `{sql_generation, findings_prose, system_prefix}` → iris file paths; PATH-EXISTENCE-VALIDATION (`gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<path>?ref=<iris-commit>`) guards against stale targets before two-phase creation.
- Types 4 and 5 are explicitly NOT auto-PR'd: Type 4 routes to a human-judgment issue (EVAL-INVISIBLE acknowledged), Type 5 to a triage-labeled issue; both go to classdojo/iris with `loop/<date>-<id>` label; PENDING-IMPLEMENTATION lifecycle is distinct from merge-landed.
- All routing artifacts (PRs, issues) target classdojo/iris; loop state and reports stay in dotdev on `loop-state`; r3 removed the spurious dotdev reference from reconcile.
- CUMULATIVE-REGRESSION banner appears in LOOP-HEALTH (§C §2), which precedes candidate processing — a health failure emits zero candidates. Cross-lane callout is a distinct section above approval commands.
- `[SOLE-DOMAIN]` and `[NEXT APPROVAL TRIGGERS BASELINE REFRESH]` are specified as interpreted flags in the per-candidate confounder card (DL-0023 §I confirmed).
- `loop approve` fails APPROVAL-DEADLINE-EXPIRED if a newer run key exists; `loop run` is manual in v1 so deadline is operator-controlled.

### Q1 — Do route targets map to actual IRIS surfaces?

**Type 1 (prompt/instruction → PR to classdojo/iris): AGREE with minor gap**
The three-key yaml → path resolution → PATH-EXISTENCE-VALIDATION chain is correct. OD-1 is explicitly OPEN and blocks Type 1 at runtime via ROUTE-TARGET-STALE. The gap: if ROUTE-TARGET-STALE fires, the approval record is already written (§D: routing executes *after* the approval record), but the design only says "abort" — it does not specify whether the candidate remains in a recoverable approved-not-yet-routed state or is stuck. No explicit retry command or runbook entry covers this case.

**Fix (minor, low risk):** Add one sentence: "On ROUTE-TARGET-STALE, the candidate remains as `approved-not-yet-landed`; operator must either (a) resolve the target yaml and re-run `loop approve <date> <id>` (routing-phase retry; approval record already exists), or (b) `loop reject <date> <id>`." The §J runbook should mirror this.

**Type 2 (habit/reflection → PR to classdojo/iris): OBJECT**
The design assumes IRIS habits/reflections are a git-tracked file in classdojo/iris that a PR can modify. DL-0023 §A.2 specifies `{scope, scope_key}` but says nothing about storage format. If IRIS habits are stored in a database, a workflow state machine, or a non-git artifact store, a git PR is structurally wrong. This is entirely gated on OD-2 — which the design acknowledges — but the failure mode is worse than documented: ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2 fires *after* the approval record is written, leaving the candidate approved-but-unrouted with no explicit recovery. The §J runbook covers only "LOOP PR FAILS IRIS CI," not "OD-2 never resolved."

**Fix:** (a) Add a pre-approval check for Type 2: before writing the approval record, verify `iris-habit-targets.yaml` is populated; if not, fail with ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2 *before* writing the record (keeps state clean). (b) Add a §J runbook entry: "If `loop approve` exits with ROUTE-UNRESOLVED-OD2: resolve OD-2 and populate `iris-habit-targets.yaml`, then re-invoke `loop approve <date> <id>` to retry routing; OR `loop reject <date> <id>` to explicitly reject."

**Type 3 (tool schema → PR to iris): AGREE**
Requires `{target_tool_path}` field; PATH-EXISTENCE-VALIDATION guards. Tool schemas are plausibly file-addressed in a real codebase. No gap beyond OD-style unknowns.

**Type 4/5 (NOT auto-PR'd → ISSUE): AGREE on direction; OBJECT on landing detection**
Routing to issues (not PRs) for EVAL-INVISIBLE retrieval corpus and code changes is correct. Label-based crash-resume (`gh issue list --label loop/<date>-<id> --state open`) is sound. The gap is in §F auto-detect landing: `gh issue list --repo classdojo/iris --label loop/<date>-<id> --state closed` cannot distinguish "implemented and closed" from "won't fix / duplicate / out-of-scope closed." A false positive increments `change-counter` and could prematurely trigger a baseline-refresh proposal.

**Fix:** Filter closed issues by a specific "implemented" close signal. Two concrete options: (1) require an `implemented` or `loop-landed` label to be present at close time (operator or dev adds it), used as the auto-detect gate; (2) document that auto-detect is a soft signal, and production landing always requires `loop mark-landed <date> <id>` with `{human_confirmed:true}` — auto-detect is only for convenience when the label was properly applied. Either way, add an explicit note to the report's STALENESS ALERT: "Auto-detected issue closes may include non-implemented closes; verify with `loop status` before relying on the counter."

---

### Q2 — Cross-repo routing: does it land in the right place?

**AGREE.**
The repo boundary is clean and consistent throughout:
- All PRs → classdojo/iris, branch `loop/<date>-<id>`, base: default-branch
- All issues → classdojo/iris, label `loop/<date>-<id>`
- PATH-EXISTENCE-VALIDATION → `gh api repos/classdojo/iris/contents/<path>?ref=<iris-commit>` ✓
- Reconcile PR scan → `gh pr list --repo classdojo/iris --head loop/… base:default-branch` (r3 fix confirmed) ✓
- Reconcile issue scan → `gh issue list --repo classdojo/iris --label loop/<date>-<id> --state closed` ✓
- Crash-resume PR probe → `--repo classdojo/iris` ✓; issue probe → `--repo classdojo/iris` ✓
- State, reports, config yamls → dotdev, `loop-state` branch ✓

One minor gap: §F reconcile dedup checks `merge {repo, sha}` but doesn't specify which SHA. Squash-merge and merge-commit produce different SHAs; `gh pr list --json mergeCommit` returns `mergeCommit.oid` (the actual commit on the default branch), which is the correct dedup key regardless of merge strategy. Worth pinning in the spec.

---

**AGREE on the conceptual model.**

**OBJECT on crash recovery from mid-`loop approve` routing failure.**
§D says the approve sequence is: (1) write approval record → (2) path-existence validation → (3) two-phase artifact creation → (4) write URL to state, all within one command invocation. A `loop run` would then start with reconcile → STALE-RUN check → but neither of these explicitly rescues a candidate stuck in `status=routing` with no URL.
